en: Mayon Volcano in Albay displays a near-perfect symmetrical cone shape that is clearly visible from the surrounding Legazpi area.
During the dry season, the grass-covered Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn brown and look like giant chocolate mounds.
Taal Volcano in Batangas features a main crater lake that contains Volcano Island, creating a lake within a lake.
Carved into the mountains of Ifugao, the Banaue Rice Terraces follow the natural contour lines of the steep slopes.
The tamaraw, found only on Mindoro island, is a small buffalo recognizable by its distinct V-shaped horns.
The Philippine eagle, native to Mindanao forests, is easily identified by its thick, shaggy crest of dark brown feathers.
At dawn, observers on Mount Pulag in Benguet can see a sea of clouds forming below the mountain's grassy peak.
Sunlight reflecting off the clear, deep water gives the Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur its striking blue color.
The beach in Santa Ana, Cagayan, displays pink sand caused by crushed red foraminifera shells mixing with white coral sand.
The Philippine tarsier, observable in the forests of Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan is a navigable underground river that flows directly into the South China Sea.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, featuring a distinct rocky summit and active fumaroles.
